text:
Andrea: Quick sync — discovered a bunch of corner cases with token stickiness at the edge when we do quota attribution + routing fallbacks. TL;DR: sticky routing helps latency but can blow a single key's quota and mess up billing attribution.
Sam: Can you give an example?
Andrea: Yeah — flow: request hits edge in region A, routed to model pool A, we mark the token as sticky to pool A for performance. Then if pool A is overloaded we fallback to pool B but still keep affinity for the token. If that token is a shared project key used widely, it eats quota on pool B until eviction.
Morgan: So sticky state survives across fallbacks? I thought we reset on fallback.
Andrea: Currently we persist a small affinity hint in the routing metadata (TTL 5m). It does not auto-clear on fallback because of simplicity. That causes skewed quota chargebacks and makes console metrics noisy.
Jamal: Oof. Two failure modes I care about: (1) quota hot-potato where one SA/key causes regional saturation, (2) billing attribution shows wrong origin when sticky persists across org boundaries.
Sam: Could we scope stickiness to "origin project" instead of raw key? Then shared keys still behave poorly.
Morgan: Another option: only make sticky for low-cardinality keys (per-key request rate < X rps) and for org-owned service accounts. Heuristic: `if key_rps < 0.5 and key_type == sa then sticky=true`
Andrea: That seems reasonable. Also consider a version that tracks fallback_count and auto-drops affinity after N fallbacks. Like: `drop_affinity_if(fallback_count >= 2)`
Jamal: What's the UX tie-in? Product wants console to show when affinity caused quota bursts. We need telemetry fields: `affinity_assigned=true`, `affinity_dropped_reason`, `fallback_count`, `effective_origin` (the pool that served the request).
Sam: Agree. Add `affinity_age_seconds` too so we can plot stickiness duration.
Morgan: For rollout, propose feature-flagged policy with 3 heuristics: 1) origin-scoped only, 2) rate-threshold based, 3) fallback-aware drop. Start with origin-scoped at 1% traffic for 48h, collect signals.
Andrea: Nice. For dashboards we should surface: per-tenant sticky_ratio, sticky_quota_delta (quota used while sticky minus expected baseline), and sticky_fallback_rate. Also an alert if sticky_quota_delta > 50% for any tenant in 1h window.
Jamal: Who owns instrumenting the metrics? Eng-platform owns routing tags, eng-sre owns alerts, product owns console panels. We need a handoff doc.
Sam: I'll add a short telemetry PR with new tags: `affinity_assigned`, `affinity_dropped`, `affinity_drop_reason`, `fallback_count`, `effective_origin`, `affinity_age`.
Andrea: Thanks. Also need a playbook: rollback if we see >5% increase in quota-exhaustion rate for top-20 tenants. That should be a circuit-breaker in the flag.
Morgan: Implementation note — KV cache currently keys on session+region; changing affinity TTL will touch cache eviction logic. Might add a cheap in-memory bloom to avoid cross-region lookups.
Jamal: Can we mitigate billing misattribution today without full stickiness rewrite? E.g., tag charge events with `claimed_origin` vs `served_origin` so billing shows both and we can reconcile.
Andrea: Yes, add `claimed_origin` (where the affinity points) and `served_origin` (where the token actually executed). Billing can prefer `served_origin` for costing and show `claimed_origin` for debugging.
Sam: I'll draft the PRs and a rollout checklist: feature-flag, 1% canary, 24h metrics review, expand to 10% and 1 week, then GA. Also include a console badge that shows "Affinity: on/auto-dropped" per key.
Morgan: FYI: ops-bot noted an alert yesterday for quota spike in us-west tied to a single SA key — probably this.
ops-bot: incident#8392 created for us-west quota spike, linked keys: sa-xx-334, current status: investigation
Andrea: Good catch. Ok owners: Sam will do telemetry PR, Morgan will prototype fallback-drop logic, Jamal will draft console spec, I'll own rollout checklist and playbook. We'll sync on Monday standup. :thumbsup:
Sam: +1
Morgan: +1
Jamal: +1
Andrea: Thanks everyone.
